headline: Tennis legend Rafael Nadal backs Spain to win World Cup 2026 final
summary: The retired sporting icon expressed confidence in 'La Roja' ahead of their blockbuster clash against Argentina, while praising the reigning champions' quality.
details: Tennis legend Rafael Nadal has thrown his support behind Spain ahead of their FIFA World Cup 2026 final clash against Argentina. The 22-time Grand Slam champion believes 'La Roja' have what it takes to lift the trophy.
Nadal shared an emotional message on social media, recalling Spain's historic 2010 World Cup triumph in South Africa. He noted that football has been one of his greatest passions since childhood.
Speaking to El Partidazo de COPE, Nadal predicted a tightly contested encounter. He noted that while Argentina is dangerous and plays to its strengths, Spain must focus on its own level to win.
The sporting icon praised the constant growth of Luis de la Fuente's side, stating that the team has reached its peak just in time for the final.
Despite his support for Spain, Nadal expressed deep respect for Argentina and their coach, Lionel Scaloni. He revealed a close personal relationship with Scaloni and many Argentine friends.
Nadal admitted that if Spain were to lose, losing to Argentina would be easier to accept because of the respect and admiration he holds for the country and its leadership.
caption:
Can Spain reclaim global glory? Tennis icon Rafael Nadal believes they can.

Tennis legend Rafael Nadal has thrown his support behind Spain ahead of their FIFA World Cup 2026 final clash against Argentina. The 22-time Grand Slam champion believes 'La Roja' have what it takes to lift the trophy.

Nadal shared an emotional message on social media, recalling Spain's historic 2010 World Cup triumph in South Africa. He noted that football has been one of his greatest passions since childhood.

Speaking to El Partidazo de COPE, Nadal predicted a tightly contested encounter. He noted that while Argentina is dangerous and plays to its strengths, Spain must focus on its own level to win.

The sporting icon praised the constant growth of Luis de la Fuente's side, stating that the team has reached its peak just in time for the final.

Despite his support for Spain, Nadal expressed deep respect for Argentina and their coach, Lionel Scaloni. He revealed a close personal relationship with Scaloni and many Argentine friends.

Nadal admitted that if Spain were to lose, losing to Argentina would be easier to accept because of the respect and admiration he holds for the country and its leadership.

headline_marked: Amit Shah visits border, [[stresses security of 'Chicken's Neck']] corridor
headline: Amit Shah visits border, stresses security of 'Chicken's Neck' corridor
summary: India's Home Minister visited the India-Bangladesh border in West Bengal, focusing on preventing infiltration and strengthening the Siliguri Corridor.
details: Indian Home Minister Amit Shah visited the India-Bangladesh border in West Bengal to review security measures. He specifically focused on the 'Chicken's Neck' or Siliguri Corridor, a narrow strip of land connecting mainland India to its northeastern states.
During his visit, Shah inspected the border areas of Dabgram-Phulbari, Jamuria Vita, and Sannyasi Kata. He also visited the Jumagach border outpost and interacted with BSF personnel.

The Home Minister inaugurated 14 new border outposts and laid the foundation for several BSF development projects. He emphasized the creation of a four-tier security ring to make the border impenetrable.
Shah held discussions with West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari regarding the security of the Siliguri Corridor. He stressed the need for modern technology to prevent infiltration.
The Siliguri Corridor, spanning 20 to 22 kilometers between Bangladesh and Nepal, is often viewed by geopolitical analysts as a strategic vulnerability for India.

This move comes amid reported tensions in Dhaka-Delhi relations following the July uprising in Bangladesh. The West Bengal government has recently provided 1,000 acres of land to the BSF for border fencing.
